data.body:
CLOSING on Gerrit change 1140 (commit b4b475b04): Verified +1, LLM-Review +1, submittable.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, each with its evidence in tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:

- a raise in the pre-call window still closes the session, and the test FAILS against the old code
  so it cannot pass vacuously: test_a_raise_in_the_pre_call_window_still_closes_the_session. It
  injects the failure at build_usage_limits (runner.py:428), which sat INSIDE the old unguarded
  window (294-444) and after provider construction. Confirmed RED before the change with exactly
  the intended message ("a raise in the pre-call window leaked the provider session's client").
- the happy path closes EXACTLY once: test_a_successful_run_closes_the_session_exactly_once. A
  `with` plus a leftover `finally: provider_session.close()` would double-close; MUTATION-VERIFIED
  by re-adding that call, which fails the test with "closed 2 times".
- `grep -c 'with ProviderSession' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is 1, and the redundant explicit close
  is gone (`grep -c 'provider_session.close()'` is 0). providers.py:18-24 no longer documents an
  absent caller.
- a close that raises is logged and never propagated: test_a_transport_close_that_raises_is_
  swallowed_by_the_session, asserted on the REAL ProviderSession with a closeable whose aclose()
  raises. NOTE this criterion was initially mis-tested by me against the STUB, demanding that
  run() swallow the error; the real contract puts best-effort teardown INSIDE close()
  (providers.py:309, "log, never raise"), so a `with` would propagate too and a49e would not have
  fixed it. Corrected to test the real object before implementation began.
- _NoBuildProviderSession gains __enter__/__exit__ in THIS commit
  (tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py), and that file passes. A stub acquiring
  the protocol the real object already has, not a weakened assertion.
- assert_gated ordering is now PROVEN, not asserted in prose:
  test_the_gate_refusal_runs_before_any_provider_client_is_built monkeypatches the gate to refuse
  and asserts NO session is ever constructed. Pinned to the gate's own LLMConfigError with a
  message match, so an unrelated early failure cannot satisfy it.
- full suite passes with no assertion weakened, skipped or deleted: 8258 passed / 74 skipped /
  0 FAILED. make lint 0, make typecheck 0.

LOC: runner.py 647 -> 647. LOC-NEUTRAL exactly as the plan projected — this swaps a
construct-plus-finally for a `with`, reindenting ~205 lines rather than adding or removing logic.

TWO THINGS FIXED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND, recorded because both were my own defects:
1. EVERY file:line citation in this plan had rotted, and I re-measured them all before writing
   code: construction 301->294, guard try 474->445, finally 582->501, providers.py dunders
   295-299 -> 323/326, assert_gated 256->261. Sibling tickets e6bd and 8229 shifted the file under
   this plan. A plan citing file:line inside a file its OWN story is rewriting will always go
   stale; the plan now instructs re-locating by CONTENT.
2. ruff B017 caught a vacuity hole in my leak test: `pytest.raises(Exception)` would have passed
   on ANY exception, including an unrelated early failure, without the leak path ever running.
   Now pinned to the injected RuntimeError with a match.

HELD-OUT TDD: 5 tests authored; the implementer was given ONE (the happy path) with the other four
removed from its tree. The two defect tests were RED first for the right reasons and are GREEN
now; the three invariant guards were green throughout and had to STAY green.
